## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40aedc58bafa4e14350af419577cd51cd82b4023`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs

PR #34133 (card #33601), GOVERNED Tier S through its one `.claude/**` path. Inputs read: the card body and its three comments (triage 6888154659, claim 6899870322, os-dev-report 6901114509), the PR body, the file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `385ea1cce5e1`, which is `origin/main` as fetched), and the check-runs on the head. The write-up the card cites (`33531-delegation-review.md`) was NOT readable at its path, so nothing here rests on it. Nothing was built, tested, re-run or ablated; the record shape was printed with `record-recognisers.mjs --template` from the `main` checkout, as the brief instructs. Every test count and ablation result below is the report's, NOT MEASURED by this review.

Findings: 1 must-fix (M1), 1 should-fix (S1), 7 nits (N1 to N7).

### ① Derived judgments

Checked against the diff, and they hold:

- Size and surface: +1238 / -128 over 6 files (the API's own counts). One governed path, `references/contract-review.md`, one line replaced, 63 lines before and after. No `.changeset/` file in the diff.
- The record stage is a conjunction read last. `lowRiskArmVerdict` pushes the stage's reasons whenever either half was handed in (`reading.record != null || reading.cardLabels != null`), so half a stage is a reason for the missing half; with nothing handed in and no pull-read reason it answers Tier H on the one `pending` reason. No branch returns Tier S without both halves read and clean.
- The four sites, each read in the code:
  - queue guard (`runGuard`): a pending entry that no approval or authorized enqueue cleared has its threads read (`readRecordThreads`), then `lowRiskRecordStage` and `readCardLabels`, then `readLowRiskTier` again; an entry still Tier H skips the record leg. Recognisers that did not load, or a thread that threw, hand in an unmeasured record, so Tier H.
  - relay (`lowRiskReadingFor`, called only from the governed-review follow-up after `pr_ready`): reads the stage through `readLowRiskRecordStage` when the first plan is pending.
  - `--pr` (`pullRecordStage`): same reader, loaded lazily; readers that did not load are unmeasured, so Tier H.
  - post-merge sweep (`readArmLanding`): the stage is read on a record that stands, on the as-landed rows, with the card's labels rebuilt as they stood at the landing; Tier H there is a BREACH flagged `stage: true`.
- Which record is read: `lowRiskRecordStage` reads the line off the comment `locateReviewOfRecord` chose, which is the NEWEST comment naming the current head on its `Head-sha:` line among rows already cut to trusted authors (the relay's login and `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`). An older head's record is absent for this head unless a `Regen-provenance:` chain carries it, and a carried record is refused by `lowRiskCarryRefusal` when a hop moved a changeset or catalog path or cannot be diffed. A newer same-head record without the line governs over an older one with it (pinned at the guard and at the relay).
- Values: `contractReviewSecurityTouching` counts every declaration line in the whole comment, fenced and quoted ones included, and reads a value only when exactly one exists, outside a fence and a quote, indented under four spaces, and exactly `no` or `yes` after stripping a bullet, bold and backticks. Missing, doubled, quoted, fenced, code-indented, trailing words, another value, `No`, a full-width colon and a near-miss key each read missing or unreadable, and the register treats everything but state `read` with value `no` as a reason. A record copied from another head names another head and is not located.
- Record author and session: the stage inherits the PASS record's trust exactly (trusted author, a `Reviewed-by:` line present, value not judged). It adds no session binding and removes none. Recorded as N7, not a regression.
- Stand-ins (brief item 3): `armSettledWithoutUnread` hands in no record and no card, so a re-read whose pull-read conditions hold comes back pending, and the added `guard.lowRiskRecordStagePending(work)` disjunct returns null (NOT MEASURED). The sweep's second read uses the real `armGit`, not `favourableArmGitRead`. No stand-in path can produce a record reading `no`. The changed line sits in `armSettledWithoutUnread`, next to and not inside `favourableArmGitRead`; PR #34115 (open, not merged at this read) edits that function, so whichever lands second resolves a textual neighbour only.
- Card timeline (brief item 2): `makeTimelineReader` throws on a non-2xx, a non-array body and a list past 1000 events; `readCardLabels` turns a throw, a missing reader or a non-list into an unmeasured timeline inside a measured reading, which the register reads as a reason. A label list that throws or is no list is unmeasured. Fails closed.
- Battery floors moved as the diff shows: register arm 74 to 95 and sweep 51 to 66; guard arm 54 to 74 and ADR 12 to 13; half-states H43 88 to 93; recognisers template 32 to 38; relay governed-review 45 to 50.

Findings:

**M1 (must-fix) — the card conjunct reads ONE card, so a `security` label on a second card the PR delivers is never read.** `deliveredCardNumber` returns only the strongest-evidence card and reports ambiguity only at EQUAL strength. A body carrying `Fixes #A` and `Part of #B` (a shape `h7PartOfWithClosingKeyword`'s own docblock calls normal and correct), or a `Fixes #A` body on a branch named for card B, derives card A; card B's labels and timeline are not read at any of the four sites, since all four go through this one derivation. With `security` on B and the reviewer's line at `no`, the arm reads Tier S. The PR body claims the conjunct for "the card the PR delivers"; the enforcement is narrower than the claim, in the direction that fails open, and no self-test row covers a PR delivering two cards at different strengths. Fix, either form: read the labels and timeline of EVERY card the PR delivers at any strength and fail on any, or read Tier H whenever more than one card is delivered. Pin it at the guard (the one reader) and in the sweep's as-landed read.

**S1 (should-fix) — a line that is nothing but a code span holding the key and the value reads `no`.** The reader strips backticks, and the row `the one bare line reads its value … behind a bullet, bold or a code span` pins a lone backticked `Security-touching: no` as `read:no`. That spelling is how the fleet MENTIONS the line: the legend, the brief and every reason the arm prints spell it in backticks. A record that mentions the line on a line of its own and states nothing reads `no`. The same record's `Head-sha:` reader already refuses a span holding the key. Fix: a span that holds the key is unreadable; keep the value-only span (key bare, value in backticks). Flip that one row.

**N1 (nit) — hidden text.** A bare line inside an HTML comment or a pre element is invisible or rendered as code on GitHub and still reads as the record's line. Only a trusted author can write it; noted for the reader's docblock, no change asked.

**N2 (nit) — the report mislabels one floor.** "brief 22 to 24" is the letter-C scope battery; the reviewer-brief battery stays at 24. Report text only.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` is correct: `scripts/pm/**` and `.claude/**` ship in no package, the diff carries no changeset, and the label is on the PR.
- `Clause-②: no` is correct: no published schema, no `packages/spec` path and no published acceptance set moves. The change narrows an internal landing gate, which is not a declared narrowing of a published contract, so no `(narrowing)` suffix is owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.
- No SQL, no query path: the push-down check has nothing to read.

### ③ Boundary flags

Template print disclosed above. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay note. Check-runs on the head at this read: 52 runs, 29 success, 21 skipped, 0 failed, 2 still running (`Live half-state sweep`, `Test Core (1/8)`). The pre-landing check needs them green.

Deviations:

1. Ablation A4 first ran as a no-op and was re-run. Accepted; both runs are reported.
2. `armRecordStageBound` (brief item 4). A correct transition rule, accepted. The queue leg checks out the merge group itself, so the landed tree's copy of the register is the rule that judged the landing. A landing on a tree that declares the stage cannot be skipped: the regex is line-anchored, the self-test holds it against this file's own source (so a rename or reformat of the declaration goes red before it can silently unbind every later landing), an unreadable tree is NOT MEASURED, and an earlier tree excuses the stage only, never the record. An old tree's skip cannot be forged by an arm PR: its paths are catalog, changeset and prose paths, so it cannot change the register in its own landed tree; a PR that removes the declaration changes the queue rule itself and is not an arm PR. The sweep is detection, the queue is the barrier.
3. A first gate run stopped and re-run on the final head. Accepted.
4. `main` merged in once. Accepted; the head's merge base is current `main`.

Open questions:

1. Card timeline read: A. It is the PR-label rule applied to the card and it fails closed. Cost accepted: a card past 1000 timeline events, or one where `security` was ever applied by mistake, stays Tier H for every PR that delivers it.
2. Template default `yes`: A, with N3. Both options fail closed.
3. No derivable card is Tier H: A. M1 extends the same reasoning to several cards.
4. An approved or enqueue-cleared arm entry prints the pending reason: A. Outcome unchanged, no reads spent. See N6 for the pin.
5. `pr_ready` requests both approvers when the record lacks the line: A (brief item 5). Consistent with the governed-landing rules: the relay asks per pull, a request is not an approval, and the relay's arm reading feeds only this follow-up, so nothing the relay lets merge changes. Consequence to know: an arm PR readied before its record exists now always summons both approvers, so the seat readies after the record, as the hand-off order already says.
6. No grace window: A. An older record states nothing about security teaching; the reviewer posts the record again with the line.
7. The landed tree decides binding: A, as judged under deviation 2.

Out-of-scope notes (brief item 7):

- `AGENTS.md` owes an edit, and `carrier: none` is not accepted. Prime Directive 14 says the arm reads S where "the seat labels unnamed security teaching" and lands on a PASS record; after this PR an arm landing also needs the record's line at `no` and a card free of the label. The rule text now understates a landing condition. Carrier: a follow-up card filed by the seat citing this record; the edit is Tier H and lands by the maintainer's hand. It cannot ride this PR without making it Tier H. Graded N4.
- `fleet-patrols.yml` owes the same one-phrase edit to its BREACH definition (a record stage at Tier H is now a BREACH). Carrier: the same follow-up card, landed at whatever tier `readWorkflowDiff` reads a comment-only workflow edit. Graded N4.
- The dead disjunct `guard.landsOnLowRiskArm(work)` in `armSettledWithoutUnread`: leaving it is right while PR #34115 is in flight. No carrier needed; whichever lands second may drop it.

**N3 (nit) — the shipped `yes` cannot be told from a stated `yes`.** The legend tells the adopting seat to add the `security` label on `yes`, the bare template prints the line on every at-tier record including non-arm ones, and a label once added keeps the PR at Tier H even after removal. An unedited paste on an arm PR therefore costs a permanent Tier H. Toward H, so accepted; a sentence telling the seat to confirm a `yes` with the reviewer before labelling would close it.

**N4 (nit) — file the follow-up card** for the two rule texts above.

### ④ Design judgment

`references/contract-review.md` (the one `hits` file; brief item 6). The reworded line holds against the code it cites: `--template` at this head prints the line under `Scope:` with value `yes`, and its legend says when `no` may be written (no changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, whatever the path is called) and what keeps Tier H. Against the card's scenario (update the template, the reference and the batteries) it is the minimum that fits the 63-line ratchet. The reference itself does not say when to write `no` or what counts as security teaching; it delegates both to the template, which is acceptable for a file under a line ratchet.

**N5 (nit) — the line gave up the two key spellings `Implemented-by:` and `Reviewed-by:`.** They remain in `lanes/review.md` and the template; the reference now names the pair only as 独立性对. Its pre-landing check line ① also does not mention the arm's line, so a seat reading only the reference learns of it from the guard's refusal. Loud, so a nit; fold into the follow-up card if a line can be found.

Implementing files: the code agrees with the contract it implements except M1 and S1.

**N6 (nit) — conjuncts with no pin found by name (brief item 8).** Beside M1's edge: in `readArmLanding`, the branch that answers NOT MEASURED when the record's line could not be read (`stage.measured !== true`), and the branch that answers NOT MEASURED on a git read that fails on the second pass; at the queue leg, an approved or enqueue-cleared arm entry spending no stage read and printing the pending reason (pinned in the sweep only). Each fails toward BREACH or leaves the outcome unchanged, so none fails open.

**N7 (nit) — the stage is as forgeable as the PASS it rides on.** Any seat can post a record through the relay under the trusted login, and the `Reviewed-by:` value is not compared to the implementer at the guard. Pre-existing and out of this card's reach; noted so the line is not read as an independence check.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-cbno0j`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmPd7uRqHauEehGPr19`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e34225e64a034d6be6eac86fbced951620c6ec8c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs

Read at 2026-11-15T22:12Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6902016216; lane request 6902008041 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's own at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#1 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla.

PR #34133 (card #33601). Read: the card body and its four comments (triage, claim, both dev reports), the PR body, the earlier record 6901227563 on head `40aedc58` (a FAIL on M1 and S1 of that round), the net diff from merge base `385ea1cce5e1` to this head over all six files, the cited code at this head (`locateReviewOfRecord`, the relation extractors, `makeTimelineReader`, the register rows, `readArmLanding`), the check-runs and the pull row. Nothing was built, tested or re-run; every test count and ablation below is the dev report's and is NOT MEASURED here.

Findings: 1 must-fix (M1), 1 should-fix (S1), 5 nits (N1 to N5).

### ① Derived judgments

Read in the code at this head, and they hold:

- Strictly a tightening on the arm. `lowRiskArmVerdict` keeps every earlier pull-read conjunct and adds reasons only. Tier S now needs a stage that was handed in and gave no reason; a reading that hands in nothing is `pending` at Tier H on one reason, and half a stage is a reason for the missing half. No branch answers Tier S that did not before. The other Tier S legs (`.claude/**`, the workflow split) are untouched: `lowRiskRecordStagePending` is false for them and `runGuard` takes its old path.
- One parser. The queue guard, the relay, `--pr` and the sweep all reach the line through `recognisers.reading`, which is `contractReviewRecordReading`; the key and the two values are exported once from `check-half-states.mjs` and re-exported by `record-recognisers.mjs`. The register's own literal `LOW_RISK_RECORD_LINE` is held to them by a self-test row.
- The line's reading fails closed. Every declaration line in the whole comment counts, fenced and quoted ones included; a value is read only from exactly one, outside a fence and a quote, indented under four columns, key outside any code span, reading exactly the key, a colon, one blank and `no` or `yes`. Read against the shapes the brief names: another case, a full-width colon, a space before the colon, trailing words, a heading mark, a numbered bullet, underscore emphasis, a tab or four-space indent, a second line, a fenced line beside a bare one — each `unreadable`; a table cell, a mid-line mention, a nested bullet pair — `missing`. Each of those is a reason in `lowRiskRecordLineReasons`; only state `read` with value `no` passes, and a null reading is "carries no line".
- Which record. The line is read off the comment `locateReviewOfRecord` chose: the newest trusted-author comment whose `Head-sha:` line names this head, PR thread or card thread. An older head's record is absent for this head. A carried record (the regeneration and prose-only hops) is re-tested by `lowRiskCarryRefusal`, now shared by the PASS and the stage: a hop that moved a `.changeset/` path or any path under a low-risk row, or that cannot be diffed, refuses. A newer same-head record without the line governs over an older one with it. The PASS and the line come from the same comment, since both legs call the one locator on the one pair.
- The card conjunct. `namedCardNumbers` lists every closing-keyword, `Part of` and `Refs` target and the protocol branch's card; `readCardLabels` reads the labels route and the timeline of each. A non-2xx, a non-array body, more than 1000 labels or timeline events, no reader, no derivable card, an `others` that does not say it was read, or more than eight other cards is each a reason. The label is matched in any case; a removed label is read from the timeline's `unlabeled` event. A label removed and put back is carried now, so it is a reason on the label list. No API error reads as "never labelled".
- The sweep. `readArmLanding`'s first read now branches on `pending` where it branched on Tier S; the two sets are the same pulls, so no earlier landing changes class. The stage is read only when the landed commit's own copy of the register declares `LOW_RISK_RECORD_STAGE` (`armRecordStageBound`, a line-anchored test held against this file's own source by a self-test row); an earlier tree is a pass on its record alone, flagged; a tree that cannot be read is NOT MEASURED; an earlier tree excuses the stage only, never the record. The low-risk rows are scoped to this repository, so no landing in another repository reaches that read. Card labels are rebuilt as they stood at the landing, an untimed event read toward BREACH.
- The relay. `lowRiskReadingFor` reads the stage only when the first plan is `pending`, through the guard's `readLowRiskRecordStage` on the relay's token, and feeds only the decision whether `pr_ready` requests the approvers. Every failure requests them. It lets nothing merge and withholds no request it sent before for a pull that is not Tier S on the full reading. Safe.
- The template. At this head `contractReviewRecordLines` prints the line after `Scope:` on the bare, rules and schema faces and, with `--paths`, exactly when a hit sits under a low-risk row; it ships `yes`, which the reader reads as `yes`. The legend and the brief name the line on the same predicate. Template, legend and reader agree on spelling; the reader accepts the line anywhere in the comment and the template places it in the header block.
- Round-1 findings: M1 of record 6901227563 is closed in code (every named card is read at all four sites, pinned at each); S1 is closed (a code span holding the key is unreadable, the row flipped).
- Pins, by name in the diff: each fail-closed branch has a refusing row and a control beside it — the record-line control and its absent, `yes`, unreadable, newest-governs, untrusted-author, unsigned and unread rows; the card-label control and its now, removed, unread and no-card rows; the named-cards control and its three relation rows, unread and over-limit rows; the `--pr` control and its rows; the relay control and its twelve plus five variants; the rule-age control with its unbound, unreadable-tree and record-less rows.

M1 (must-fix) — this head does not merge into `main`, and the conflict sits in the reader this PR extends. GitHub answers `mergeable: false`, state `dirty`, for the pull. `main` is at `86350e12` (PR #34054), eight commits past this head's merge base `385ea1cc`; that commit rewrites the loop of `contractReviewRecordReading` and inserts eleven H43 rows directly above the `#33604 reading` row this PR re-pins, and it edits the guard's self-test as well. The round-2 report's sentence that `main` moved only by product commits touching no file of this PR is contradicted by that commit. Because the pull conflicts, no workflow ran: the head has 0 check-runs, so none of the five self-test batteries and none of the gates has been run by CI on this tree, and none will until the head moves. The tree reviewed here is therefore not a tree that can land. Fix: merge current `main`, resolve `check-half-states.mjs` (the reading's return line and the H43 rows, with the floor comment restated on the merged count), re-run the five self-tests and the gate list on the merged head, push. The merged head earns a delta review that reads the merged reader, on green checks.

S1 (should-fix) — the PR body states behaviour the code at this head does not have, in the block the maintainer reads first. (a) "What changes" item 1 lists a bulleted line among the unreadable shapes; the reader reads a bulleted line and a row pins it as `read:no`. It omits the key inside a code span, which is unreadable. (b) Item 2, the acceptance notes and the quick-read block say the card the PR delivers; the code reads every card the PR names, with a limit of eight others. (c) The tests table, the floors and the ablation list are round 1's. The dev listed these corrections for the seat; the body is unchanged at this read. Write them in the round that merges `main`.

N1 (nit) — the card conjunct is bound to the PR body as it reads at the queue, not as it read at the review. The body is the only carrier of a card relation (commit messages may not carry one), a thread-mode branch names no card, and the body can be rewritten after the record is posted, so the label read follows whatever card the body names then; a relation spelled as an issue URL or outside the four spellings names no card. Only a writer the guard already trusts with the record itself can do this, so it is the same trust the PASS rides on and no regression. Stated so the conjunct is not read as tamper-proof where the timeline read might suggest it; the path is in the seat's notes, not here.

N2 (nit) — `makeTimelineReader` ends its walk at the first page shorter than `per_page`. On a card's timeline, where the arm now reads a removed label, a short page that is not the last would end the walk early and read "never removed". Whether the timeline route answers short non-final pages was NOT MEASURED here. Following the `Link` header would not depend on it. The reader predates this PR; the card is a new consumer.

N3 (nit) — the reader is not a renderer, as its docblock says for an HTML comment and a `pre` element. One more shape of the same kind: a bare line directly under a quoted line, with no blank between, is rendered by GitHub inside the quote and reads here as the record's own line. Trusted author only; a sentence in the docblock is enough.

N4 (nit) — the sweep lists the named cards from the PR body as it reads at sweep time, while labels and comments are rebuilt as landed. A body edited after the landing changes which cards the sweep reads. Detection only; the queue read the body it had.

N5 (nit) — the reference line. It gave up the two key spellings of the independence pair, and its closing clause about the adopting seat now follows two subjects where it is true of one. The round-2 report sends the wording to the follow-up card; accepted.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` is right: `scripts/pm/**` and `.claude/**` ship in no package, the diff carries no changeset, the label is on the pull.
- `Clause-②: no` is right: no published schema, no `packages/spec` path, no published acceptance set moves. The change narrows an internal landing gate, which is not a declared narrowing of a published contract.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No SQL and no query path, so the push-down check has nothing to read.
- CI on this head: 0 check-runs and no commit status. The pull is a draft and GitHub reads it `mergeable: false`, `dirty`. Nothing is running and nothing will start on this head; see M1. This is not a "wait for the checks" state.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Disclosed: the record shape was printed with `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` from the session's checkout as the brief instructs; that checkout predates this PR, so its print carries no line for the arm. What the template prints at this head was read in the diff.
- This record carries no line for the arm, and none is owed: the PR's one governed path sits on the `.claude/**` row, which is no low-risk row, so the PR is not an arm PR and the head's own `--template --paths` prints no such line for it.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no off-relay note.
- The earlier record on this PR (6901227563) was rendered in the dispatching account's own session and is on an older head; this review rests on none of its conclusions and re-read each one it cites.
- Deviations of round 2: the wider card set (every named card, not every delivered one), the over-limit landing read as a stage BREACH, the approval-cleared entry stopping one conjunct earlier, N5 and N7 of the earlier record left — each accepted as reported. Not accepted: "main moved by three product commits that touch no file of this PR" (M1).
- Open questions of round 2: 1 A (a label is not a thread; one card too many fails closed). 2 A (eight; a bounded cost in the merge group). 3 A (the queue counted the same names and refused). 4 A (a key in a span is the mention spelling). 5 A (no renderer in the reader; see N3).
- Out of scope, with a carrier: AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14 still says only that the seat labels unnamed security teaching, and the sweep job's comment in `fleet-patrols.yml` still defines a BREACH without the record stage. Both are Tier H texts this PR cannot touch and stay off Tier H; the carrier is comment 6901240370 on card #33768, read and found to name both edits. No register row and no hook roster needs a matching change: no governed path is added or moved.

### ④ Design judgment

`references/contract-review.md` (the one `hits` file). The reworded line holds against the code it cites: at this head `--template` prints the line and its legend says when `no` may be written and what keeps Tier H. Against the card's scenario it is the minimum that fits the file's 63-line ratchet; the reference delegates the values to the template, which is acceptable for a file under a line budget. N5 stands on it.

Implementing files, against the contract they implement (the card: one machine-read line, absent or unreadable or anything but `no` is Tier H, the label on the linked card is read, the template, the reference and the batteries move):

- `check-half-states.mjs`: the reader does what the card asks and no reading defaults to `no`.
- `record-recognisers.mjs`: the template emits the line where an arm PR can sit and ships the failing value; `namedCardNumbers` is wider than the delivery relation on purpose and says so.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: one stage reader for every site; the carry rule is one function for the PASS and the stage.
